name: IRIS RegTech Solutions Ltd
title: IRIS RegTech Solutions Ltd - 540735 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Software/RegTech call with no capacity or utilisation content; management guides INR500 crore revenue aspiration (~30% CAGR over 4-5 years), IRIS CARBON ARR growth ~35% target, and flags possible Middle East SupTech pipeline delay after June.

triggers.label: INR500 cr revenue aspiration reiterated
triggers.quote: In short, the target is INR500 crores, and we feel we are getting into a position

triggers.label: Middle East SupTech pipeline risk
triggers.quote: I wouldn't be surprised if there is some delay if this whole thing continues beyond a point.

guidance.quote: this will require a growth rate of slightly over 30%over the next 4 to 5 years
For our SaaS business, we are targeting an ARR growth rate of approximately 35%
I would say that 75 to 80 days is what we would be comfortable

red_flags.label: Middle East SupTech pipeline risk
red_flags.quote: it is possible that a prolonged Middle East crisis might have a possible adverse impact on the SupTech pipeline.

red_flags.label: Sales spend elevated for growth
red_flags.quote: We are well below the SaaS benchmarks where people spend at times more than $2 for $1 of net ARR. We are at about 1.1, 1.2 levels.

evasions.quote: we are setting the conditions for reaching this target
nothing is off the table, but we'll be disciplined

summary.headline: IRIS RegTech targets INR500 crore revenue, needing ~30%+ growth over 4-5 years; FY26 revenue grew ~23% with EBITDA margin ~14%.
summary.overview: Management framed FY26 as steady: total revenue grew about 23% and EBITDA margin was about 14%, with management asking analysts to judge the business on annual rather than quarterly numbers. IRIS CARBON ARR grew 33% on disclosure-management wins and iDEAL ARR grew 17%, while SupTech added 3 new logos including the Government of Qatar. Post the TaxTech divestment, cash was about INR155 crore and net worth rose to INR200 crore from INR76 crore. Management reiterated the INR500 crore revenue aspiration and said the Middle East crisis is a watch item rather than a current drag.

financial_highlights.change: From INR76 crore as at March 31, 2025
Delayed Indian customer decisions in H1 FY26

segments.name: RegTech - IRIS CARBON (SaaS, enterprise)
segments.commentary: ARR grew 33% on disclosure-management wins; ESG reporting module launched as an add-on. Management targets about 35% ARR growth and says it is breaking into large enterprise accounts. Sales and marketing spend is planned to be stepped up in a measured way, at about 1.1-1.2x net ARR, and kept EBITDA positive.

segments.name: RegTech - IRIS iDEAL (BFSI automated regulatory reporting)
segments.commentary: ARR grew 17% despite slower Indian purchase decisions in H1 FY26. Company is exploring Africa and Middle East, with some Europe interest; revenue mix is subscription, implementation and licence.

segments.name: SupTech - iFile
segments.commentary: Added 3 new logos in FY26, including Government of Qatar for tax reporting, plus a deposit insurance management segment. Product suite is being extended to licensing, risk-based supervision, case management and decision management. Revenue is lumpier and expected to grow slower than SaaS; management expects 3-4 SupTech wins in a typical year.

segments.name: DataTech / IRIS Peridot (MSME)
segments.commentary: Spun off into a subsidiary for sharper focus. Loan facilitation piloted from February 2026 with 3 lenders onboarded so far; monetisation is at an early stage and management's internal target is earlier than the 2-year horizon an analyst suggested.

guidance_outlook: Revenue aspiration of INR500 crore, which management says needs growth slightly over 30% over the next 4-5 years.
SaaS ARR growth target of about 35% (stated externally), with management saying internally it could be higher.
SupTech expected to grow at a lower rate than SaaS, with possible lumpy upside.
Sales and marketing to rise in a measured way, with IRIS CARBON the main beneficiary; company intends to stay EBITDA positive.
Receivable days (DSO) comfortable at 75-80 days; further improvement expected to be progressively difficult unless enterprise SaaS accelerates.
Some cash to be retained for possible inorganic opportunities in RegTech adjacencies; no acquisition announced.
capex_capacity: No specific capex or capacity figures were discussed.
Cash of ~INR155 crore is being deployed into CARBON sales and marketing, with the balance held back for potential inorganic deals.
Planned on-ground sales and marketing hires in developed markets (US and Europe), started recently.
Moved to a new corporate office in Turbhe, Navi Mumbai.
demand_pricing: Disclosure-management category in US and Europe described as young, with many structured-data reporting prospects; US and Europe are the priority geographies for CARBON.
Customers are excited about AI and inquiries are rising; management says it has not yet seen enterprises building in-house software or AI-native entrants in its markets.
SupTech demand linked to regulator digitisation push; some Middle East pipeline is in discussion and could slip if the crisis extends beyond about June 2026.
Regulators show reluctance on cloud-based and generic AI for confidential data; company is exploring private or sovereign small language models. PFRDA is on a private cloud.
SaaS business is mainly Europe and US, so limited direct Middle East exposure per management.

qa_highlights.question: What is the roadmap to the INR500 crore revenue target and by when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the INR500 crore aspiration, which needs growth slightly above 30% over 4-5 years. SaaS ARR targeted at about 35% growth; SupTech to grow slower, with possible surprises.

qa_highlights.question: How is AI helping, and does it raise competitive intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees AI as both opportunity and threat; it is building AI offerings and embedding AI in the development process. No competitive intensity increase seen so far from enterprises building in-house or AI-native entrants.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Middle East crisis on the year?
qa_highlights.answer: SaaS impact seen as minimal given Europe and US focus. SupTech pipeline linked to Middle East regulators could see delays if the crisis persists beyond roughly June; 3-4 SupTech wins still expected.

qa_highlights.question: Use of the cash balance: M&A, product or marketing spend?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic growth first. Sales and marketing at about 1.1-1.2x net ARR, possibly a bit higher, with no EBITDA-negative mode. Inorganic options are open but disciplined; some capital to be retained.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ~30% growth be achieved: markets, products, headcount?
qa_highlights.answer: CARBON is the flagship with ESG added; adjacencies in capital-markets and energy reporting are early. iDEAL to expand into Africa, Middle East and Europe. iFile adding licensing, risk-based analytics and case management. Developed-market sales hiring has started.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivable days falling and what is the comfort level?
qa_highlights.answer: Driven by enterprise SaaS mix rising and regulators paying promptly. Management says 75-80 days is comfortable; further improvement is progressively harder.

risks_watch: Middle East crisis could delay SupTech wins if it extends beyond roughly June 2026; government budgets may be hit by high oil prices.
Enterprise SaaS and AI disruption: management acknowledges volatility in enterprise software valuations and AI impact is uncertain.
Sales and marketing step-up at CARBON could pressure EBITDA margin from the ~14% base.
Peridot/MSME loan facilitation is at pilot stage with only 3 lenders; monetisation is unproven.
Regulator reluctance to adopt cloud and generic AI for confidential data may slow SupTech and AI-led product uptake.
Deployment of the ~INR155 crore cash into inorganic deals is undefined.
summary.management_tone: Confident on SaaS growth and balance sheet, but cautious on the Middle East and AI, with management saying it is watchful but not unduly worried. Answers on M&A and the INR500 crore timeline were measured and non-committal on dates.
key_quotes: And we're already seeing 33% ARR growth, and we want to up it as we go forward.
We don't want to do a deal just because we have the capital.
We don't want to be doing this in EBITDA negative mode.
So I would start getting worried post June, I would say.

growth.why: Management reiterated a INR500 crore revenue aspiration needing slightly over 30% growth over 4-5 years and a ~35% SaaS ARR growth target, backed mainly by stated demand, sales hiring in US/Europe and cash, with no specific capacity, orders or contracts quantified.
